title: Control Evidence Object Model
description: Generated mechanically from the CEOM v0.9.10 specification. Field names, labels and definitions are taken verbatim from the specification. Field TYPES and CARDINALITY are not stated in the specification and are therefore absent here: every such field carries "x-ceom-type-unstated": true. Deciding those types is design work, not conversion work, and is the only remaining step to a usable schema.

Obligation.title: 1 Obligation
Obligation.description: A single discrete requirement, derived from a regulatory or contractual source.

id.title: Identifier
id.description: Stable identifier for this record. Names an identity, not a row.

derived_from.title: Derived from
derived_from.description: The object or Asset this record was made from. Null means nobody could say where it came from. A record cannot evidence the thing it was derived from.

effective_from.title: Effective from
effective_from.description: When the fact it asserts began to hold.

effective_to.title: Effective to
effective_to.description: When it ceased to hold. Null means current.

source_ref.title: Source
source_ref.description: The registered Asset the requirement is published in — a rulebook, a standard, a code of practice, a contract. **Must resolve to a registered Asset**, not free text.
source_ref.x-ceom-resolve-as-at: the referring record's event time, per design principle 9

source_locator.title: Where in the source
source_locator.description: The citation within that document, as the source itself numbers it. "Principle 3, paragraph 36(c)". "Article 111".

source_version.title: Source version
source_version.description: The version of the requirement identified by `source_ref` and `source_locator` together, as that source identifies it — a version number where the source has one, a date-state where it does not. Positions within one document are amended on different dates, so this belongs to the position rather than to the document.

in_force_from.title: In force from
in_force_from.description: The date the obligation comes into effect. Not the date its source was published, which is frequently much earlier and is a fact about the document rather than about the requirement.

introduced_by.title: Introduced by
introduced_by.description: The publication that brought it in — a policy statement, consultation outcome or technical standard. How regulatory change functions actually track it.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

items.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or one of the three supranational codes.

jurisdiction.x-ceom-note: D82: coded, not free text, because comparing the six location facts against each other is the purpose of the structure. Recorded at the precision the answer was given: a provider that says "EU" is recorded as EU, and that imprecision is the finding.

applicability.title: Who it applies to
applicability.description: Which entities, products and transactions the obligation binds.

part_of.title: Part of
part_of.description: The parent Obligation this one decomposes. Optional, resolved as at `effective_from` under principle 9.

owner_id.title: Obligation owner
owner_id.description: The firm's owner of this obligation record. Accountable for it being correctly stated, correctly scoped, and still current. Not for the requirement existing.
owner_id.x-ceom-resolve-as-at: the referring record's event time, per design principle 9

established_by.title: Who determined it was needed
established_by.description: The person or system that decided this grantee should hold this. Often the grantee themselves, which is itself a finding.
established_by.x-ceom-note: Typed actor: actor_type from human/system/agent plus a reference. human resolves to an Owner as at effective_from; system and agent resolve to an Asset.

established_from.title: What they relied on
established_from.description: The Asset relied upon — a contract, a role record, a screening report, a change ticket. **Null means the grant rests on assertion alone.**

approved_by.title: Who accepted it
approved_by.description: **Must differ from `established_by`.** Self-approval is not approval. Null is a finding, not a blank.

approved_from.title: What the approver relied on
approved_from.description: The Asset the approver relied upon. Distinct from `established_from`, which is what the establisher relied upon. **Null means the approval rests on nothing recorded.**

enforced_by.title: Enforced in
enforced_by.description: The Asset that enforces the grant — an IAM policy, an access gateway, or the application itself. Resolved as at `effective_from` under principle 9.

source_ref.title: Source document
source_ref.description: The Asset the grant is recorded in. **Must resolve to a registered Asset**, not free text.
source_ref.x-ceom-resolve-as-at: the referring record's event time, per design principle 9

statement.title: The constraint
statement.description: The rule in words. "Transactions at or above the threshold require human approval."

value.title: Value as observed
value.description: The threshold at the moment it was recorded. Null where the constraint has no number.

value_ref.title: Where the value is maintained
value_ref.description: The Asset holding the configured value. **Must resolve to a registered Asset.** Null means the number is maintained nowhere, or nobody could say where.
value_ref.x-ceom-resolve-as-at: the referring record's event time, per design principle 9
